items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I remember I was a member of the BMI Writers Workshop in New York with Bob Brookmeyer and Manny Albam.

ctx.x: There’s a lot to be said for that, develop your own style. I think the things you learn to do and not to do really make a strong impression on you when you’re trying it on your own. Your friend and sometimes bandmate Alan Broadbent described that when you bring in an arrangement and you hear it for the first time, he called it the “cringe moment.”

Also the joy moment. It’s so great to – especially if you’re working with a big band or orchestra like Alan does a lot and I do from time to time. It’s such a joy to hear it with live instruments. Now we can mock it up on synthesizers and before, in the old days, we couldn’t. We just played and heard it on the piano. But it’s the cringe moment but also joyous when it all comes together and it works. And you know it’s great, we had workshops back in the day, I remember I was a member of the BMI Writers Workshop in…
When you were in your teens, after the banjo experience, did you have a choice of what you were going to do with your life? Did you have something to decide? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
